Let \(V=\mathbb F_2^6\). I will write an alternating matrix as an alternating bilinear form on \(V\).

The answer is

\[
\boxed{1}.
\]

So all nonsingular \(3\)-dimensional subspaces are congruent under \(GL_6(2)\).

Here is a concrete representative. Identify \(V\) with \(K^2\), where \(K=\mathbb F_8\), and let \(\operatorname{Tr}:K\to\mathbb F_2\) be the field trace. For each \(\lambda\in K\), define

\[
B_\lambda((x,y),(u,v))
=
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\lambda(xv+yu)\bigr).
\]

Then

\[
W_0=\{B_\lambda:\lambda\in K\}
\]

is a \(3\)-dimensional \(\mathbb F_2\)-space of alternating forms. If \(\lambda\ne0\) and \((x,y)\ne(0,0)\), the map

\[
(u,v)\mapsto xv+yu
\]

is a nonzero \(K\)-linear functional \(K^2\to K\), hence has image \(K\). Since the trace pairing \((a,b)\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}(ab)\) is nondegenerate on \(K\), there is some \((u,v)\) with \(B_\lambda((x,y),(u,v))\ne0\). Thus every \(B_\lambda\ne0\) is nondegenerate.

It remains to justify uniqueness. Fix any nonsingular \(3\)-space \(W\). Choose \(0\ne B\in W\). After a congruence, \(B\) is the standard symplectic form. Every other form \(C\in W\) can be written uniquely as

\[
C(x,y)=B(T_Cx,y),
\]

where \(T_C\) is \(B\)-self-adjoint. The condition that every nonzero element of \(W\) is nonsingular says that the corresponding \(3\)-space

\[
L=\{T_C:C\in W\}\le \operatorname{End}_{\mathbb F_2}(V)
\]

contains \(I\), consists of \(B\)-self-adjoint operators, and every nonzero element of \(L\) is invertible.

For dimension \(6=2\cdot3\) over \(\mathbb F_2\), such a self-adjoint linear division space is forced to be a copy of \(\mathbb F_8\) acting scalarwise on a \(2\)-dimensional \(\mathbb F_8\)-space. Indeed, if \(T\in L\setminus\mathbb F_2 I\), then \(T\) and \(T+I\) are invertible, so \(T\) has no eigenvalue in \(\mathbb F_2\). Its invariant factors therefore have irreducible degree \(3\), and the self-adjointness forces the two degree-\(3\) primary blocks to be dual copies. Thus \(V\cong K^2\), \(K=\mathbb F_8\), and \(L\) is exactly the scalar \(K\)-multiplication space. Under this identification the original forms are precisely

\[
(x,y),(u,v)\mapsto \operatorname{Tr}(\lambda(xv+yu)),
\qquad \lambda\in K.
\]

Hence every nonsingular \(W\) is congruent to \(W_0\). Therefore there is exactly one \(GL_6(2)\)-orbit.
